_about: Voice C (task 756). Scripted answers about the recorded day in assets/judge/real_day.jsonl. 'rows' are 1-based line numbers in that file; tools/voice_judges/voicec.py checks every citation and writes the quoted rows to runs/voice/voiceC/answer_sources.json. 'keys' are phrases the matcher scores (weight after the colon, default 1). Each answer is pre-rendered to res/raw/voice_<id>.wav.

matcher._about: Task 946. Words are lower-cased, fillers dropped, stemmed (-ing/-ed/-s) and mapped through synonyms, on transcripts and keys alike. Score = key phrases + a BM25-style overlap with each answer's keys and text. A key score at threshold with a clear margin answers; a weaker but real overlap plays the nearest answer and then 'suggest'; nothing in common, or an out_of_scope phrase, plays 'fallback' (which says honestly what I know).

Ask me about this recorded day. For example: what needs me, what got built, what failed, or what happened overnight.

This is a real day of AI coding agents at work, recorded on November third. Six projects, from this headset app to geothermal fault maps. The agents planned, built and tested on their own, and by evening three questions blocked their work.

Three direction questions block their work. Geothermal faults: which mapping approach; the agents recommend adding lidar features. The agent challenge: which direction; they recommend a second, small-model entry. And the headset project: what to build by November eighteenth; they recommend this app, Flowstate.

Only new faults score; a miss costs four false alarms; the one team sharing its method used lidar for top five. A better model wins four or five of 124 agent tasks, making the bonus entry cheap upside. Flowstate already had two working headset slices.

Three tasks failed, and none was the agents' fault. Twice the geothermal data check ran before the data had been downloaded. And the first install on the headset failed because no headset was plugged in and no build existed yet.

Twenty two tasks finished. Fifteen on the headset: event format, experience design, a sound set, and a web version with a 3D task graph. Six on geothermal faults, including the real data check and training setup. The last, late afternoon, was the geothermal feature stack.
Geothermal faults is furthest along: its data, scorer, features, model and submission pieces are all built, and its training passed a GPU check. The headset project finished the most tasks: fifteen.

Geothermal faults is the riskiest: its data check failed twice, and it can't start GPU training until you pick an approach. The headset project is close behind: its deadline is November eighteenth and its direction is still open.

Work began just before 2 a.m. Within about two hours agents finished twelve of dozens of tasks, then paused. Two GPU jobs finished unattended. They restarted in the afternoon, finished ten more, and by evening three direction questions blocked their work. About nineteen hours total.

Right now the geothermal agents have structure features queued next, the agent challenge just confirmed its portal access, and the headset project is waiting on your direction question. Three smaller projects are paused.

Each project has a Head agent that plans and Workers that build, with a Chief over all. That afternoon six workers ran: three headset, two agent challenge, one geothermal. The headset agents worked hardest: three hundred and thirty two events, fifteen finished tasks.

Geothermal faults is a mapping challenge: find faults from geophysics rasters and lidar elevation maps. Only new faults score, and a miss costs four times a false alarm. Agents built the scorer, data check and features, and now wait for you to pick an approach.

The headset project is building Flowstate, this app, for a competition due November eighteenth. Today it finished the event format, the experience design, a sound set, and a web version with a 3D task graph. It is waiting on your choice of direction.

The agent challenge builds a coding agent that solves programming tasks in about five minutes each. A first entry is built and validated. The agents recommend adding a second, small-model entry for a bonus prize.
The graph shows the parts of a project. Green is built, blue is being built, amber is blocked, and grey is planned. Pinch a part to see who built it and when.
It's real. Everything here comes from a recorded day of real agents on November third. Private names are hidden, and nothing is live.
